doc.title: Billy Taylor interviewed by Michael Woods, New York City, New York, July 27, 1995

title: Treatment after earning the doctorate
summary: Taylor jokes about being called Dr. before and Bill after, and finding sloppy research in jazz writing.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: A couple of other questions. This is marvelous. Do you feel that or can you give us specific examples, do you feel you were treated different or better after you finished your doctorate? And how? When did people begin to listen to —

One of the funniest things to me, when I was working on my doctorate I was introduced to people as Dr. So-and-so, Dr. Such-and-such. As soon as I got mine it was Jim, Bill, I mean all of that stuff — I mean thanks a lot, yeah, okay. I didn’t know any more than I did before. Yes I was treated differently. Because it was an unusual thing for a jazz musician to have an earned doctorate. And I rubbed people’s noses in it. Because there was so much, when I was working on my doctorate there was so much that I found that was — well— sloppy research.
